name: Gambler
flavor: The card-sharp's discipline: a Joker who trusts the deck more than his own hands, having learned exactly which rolls can be nudged in his favor, which bets are worth doubling, and which are strictly for suckers.

features.name: Stacked Deck
features.description: You've learned to load the deck in your favor. {{uses per combat|1 at levels 1-4, 2 at 5-10, 3 at 11-16, 4 at 17+ — the same breakpoints the Scaling Die uses}} times per combat, you can do one of the following, no action required: choose the result of a Wild Card draw instead of rolling the d8; reroll a d20 you just rolled for your own attack roll, ability check, or saving throw and use the new result; or target one creature within 30 feet of you that just made an attack roll or saving throw, forcing it to succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your gambit DC or reroll that d20 and use the new result. These uses cost no Mayhem and draw on nothing else you have.
features.narration: The deck was never honest and neither were you. When the moment matters you simply arrange for the result you needed — or reach across the table and make somebody else take theirs again, which is worse.
features.sheetSummary: Choose one: pick a Wild Card result instead of rolling; reroll your own d20 attack, check, or save and use the new result; or force a creature that just rolled a d20 to make a Charisma save vs {{gambit DC|8 + proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier}} or reroll and use the new result. Costs no Mayhem.

meta.save: Cha save vs {{gambit DC|8 + proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier}} (forced reroll)

features.name: Double Down
features.description: You can bet on your own luck before you know how a roll lands. Once per turn, before making an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw (not a Parry roll), you can spend 1 Mayhem to roll a d6 and add it to the total. If that d6 comes up a 1, the bet turns on you: you take [[1d4]] psychic damage as the trick backfires, in addition to whatever the roll itself produces. You must decide to Double Down before the roll's outcome is known.
features.narration: You commit before you know. The bet goes down while the outcome is still in the air, and most of the time it comes back better than it had any right to. Occasionally it turns on you, and the recoil of it hurts somewhere behind your eyes.
features.sheetSummary: Declared before the roll. Add a d6 to an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw (never a Parry). If the d6 comes up 1, you take [[1d4]] psychic damage.

features.name: Card Sharp
features.description: You've sat at every kind of table and walked away from all of them ahead. By handling the pieces, you instantly recognize loaded dice, marked cards, or any rigged game of chance. In games of chance or gambling skill against nonmagical opposition you have advantage on any check involved, and you can cheat without being caught by anything short of magic (opposed Sleight of Hand checks made to cheat are rolled with advantage). You also have advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks to tell whether someone is bluffing about a bet, a deal, or a debt.
features.narration: You have sat at every kind of crooked table there is and walked away from all of them ahead. Loaded dice announce themselves in your palm, marked cards feel wrong on the shuffle, and nobody has ever caught you doing what you are doing.
features.sheetSummary: Auto-detect rigged games by handling them. Advantage on game-of-chance checks and on cheating undetected (vs nonmagical opposition). Advantage on Insight vs bluffs in bets, deals, and debts.
